scope: Strictly subcritical n=10 lower bound; choose a nonzero minimizing physical stress component.

statuses.hand: closed by reviewed hand deduction, with cited imported dependencies
statuses.computer: closed by reviewed computer-assisted theorem; hand replacement open

cases.title: Acyclic positive component
cases.scope: Every nonzero tree component.

cases.title: Entirely loaded cyclic component that is not a seven-body simple cycle
cases.scope: The all-loaded reduction forces an enclosing seven-cycle in a strictly subcritical ten-packing.

cases.title: Seven loaded bodies with a common signed frame offset
cases.scope: Includes the smooth uniform ring and the radial-side/diagonal endpoints.

cases.title: Nonuniform strict one-chirality seven-ring
cases.scope: After C02: the fixed side/vertex pattern, allowing reflection and cyclic relabeling. A hand cap theorem traps all three inner squares below the three-square minimum radius.

cases.title: Other seven-loaded-ring contact ownership
cases.scope: After C02 and C03: other vertex/edge ownership, geometric circle-contact types, or boundary degeneracies.

cases.title: Mixed cyclic component whose whole graph is not a simple cycle
cases.scope: Includes branching cyclic blocks and bridges attached to cyclic blocks; two loaded bodies are allowed here.

cases.title: Mixed simple cycle of length at most four
cases.scope: All load assignments.

cases.title: Mixed simple cycle of length at least five with at most two loads
cases.scope: The two-terminal transmission-path theorem applies to a whole simple cycle.

cases.title: Five-cycle with three loads and adjacent unloaded bodies
cases.scope: The middle loaded body touches every other loaded body.

cases.title: Three-loaded five-cycle with radial-side central body
cases.scope: Nonadjacent unloaded bodies; the central loaded square has two geometric circle vertices. S-S, mixed S-D, and D-D are all excluded.

cases.title: Unique-circle-vertex central body: parallel transmissions
cases.scope: Nonadjacent unloaded bodies; apply this predicate before C11–C17.

cases.title: Unique-circle-vertex central body: coincident contacts
cases.scope: After C10; equal and mixed transmission types are excluded.

cases.title: Unique-circle-vertex central body: two distinct vertex contacts
cases.scope: After C10–C11.

cases.title: Unique-circle-vertex central body: two side-normal transmissions
cases.scope: After C10–C12; includes two side-interior contacts.

cases.title: Remaining vertex/side pattern: D-D
cases.scope: First letter is the transmitter at the central vertex contact; second is at the side-interior contact.

cases.title: Remaining vertex/side pattern: S-S
cases.scope: Same ordered convention as C14; vertex exclusions and an analytic side-interior clearance proof rule out the entire S-S pattern.

cases.title: Remaining vertex/side pattern: S-D
cases.scope: Same ordered convention; physical torque balance forces a far vertex to carry circle load, while elementary analytic bounds place it strictly inside the circle.

cases.title: Remaining vertex/side pattern: D-S
cases.scope: Same ordered convention; endpoint classification and a printed exact clearance table exclude both remaining circle-load patterns.

cases.title: Five-cycle with four loads: side transmitter
cases.scope: Its only unloaded body is a degree-two side transmitter.

cases.title: Five-cycle with four loads: diagonal transmitter
cases.scope: The diagonal transmitter contains zero, lies wholly in squared radius 3/2, and permits at most one other square wholly inside the test disk; completion capacity remains open.

cases.title: Mixed simple cycles of lengths six through ten
cases.scope: At least three loaded bodies; finite cyclic load words with S/D transmission decorations.
